home.title: You see the price before you talk to us.
home.lead: Our prices are published. Answer a few questions and you get your range; the proposal then fixes it as one written figure.
home.figureNote: The estimate you would see on screen — before any call, form or meeting.

estimate.label: Your estimate
estimate.note: Every answer shows what it changed.

pay.label: What you pay
pay.note: Fixed in the proposal after a scope review. Only this one is binding.

hero.lead: Every range is on this page, by project type and complexity, with what a build includes, what is billed separately and how you pay. Your own estimate takes a few minutes; the written proposal fixes one figure.

invest.title: What it costs
invest.lead: A published figure for every service. Build prices are ranges until the proposal fixes one figure.

includes.title: What the price includes
includes.lead: What the proposal figure pays for, and what appears on its own line so nothing is folded into it.

terms.title: Payment and terms
terms.lead: How you pay, what the warranty covers and when the code becomes yours. The same terms apply to every project.

how.title: How pricing works
how.lead: One project, from the first conversation to the binding figure. Each stage publishes a narrower range; only the proposal fixes one number.

cost.title: What changes the price
cost.lead: Four answers move your estimate. Integrations and performance targets are checked with you and priced in the proposal. Maintenance is billed monthly or yearly, outside the build.

requirements.name: Requirements
requirements.does: You describe the problem and what the site or system has to do.

scope.name: Scope
scope.does: What gets designed, engineered and integrated sets the project type.

complexity.name: Complexity
complexity.does: Logic, templates, states and roles place it in a published range.

estimate.name: Estimate
estimate.does: Content, brand readiness and timeline adjust the range. Indicative, never a quotation.

proposal.name: Proposal
proposal.does: Scope review confirms integrations and performance targets, then one written figure, valid {days} days.
proposal.figure: One figure, set after scope review

moves.title: Moves your estimate
moves.lead: The estimator prices these four. Its range opens wide and narrows with every answer.

review.title: Settled in scope review
review.lead: A form cannot judge these, so the estimator leaves them out. We check them with you, and the proposal prices them.

monthly.title: Billed monthly or yearly
monthly.lead: After launch, only if you want it. Never part of the build figure.

scope.name: Scope
scope.line: What gets designed, engineered and integrated.

complexity.name: Complexity
complexity.line: How much logic, how many templates, states and roles.

content.name: Content
content.line: Whether copy, imagery and brand identity are ready.

integrations.name: Integrations
integrations.checked: Which gateway, CRM or APIs — and who owns each account. What data moves between systems, and what happens when one fails.

performance.name: Performance
performance.line: Performance, accessibility, SEO and infrastructure targets.
performance.checked: Speed and Core Web Vitals targets. Accessibility level and SEO baseline. Hosting and infrastructure.

interface.name: Website design
interface.covers: Interface and experience design, delivered as screens and a working design system.
interface.how: Per project, from the screens and flows involved

development.name: Website and web app development
development.covers: Websites and web apps built from your requirements.
development.how: Published range by project type and complexity; fixed in the proposal
development.allPrices: All {count} prices, by project type and complexity

audit.name: Technical audit
audit.covers: Architecture, performance and security review with a remediation roadmap, in {duration}.
audit.how: Fixed fee, credited to the build

maintenance.name: Website maintenance
maintenance.covers: Updates, monitoring, backups and edit requests after launch.

terms.warrantyNote: {days} days after launch — defects in delivered work are fixed at no charge.
terms.currencyNote: Invoiced in EGP for clients in Egypt and in USD for international clients.

included.title: Included in every build
included.lead: What the proposal figure pays for, phase by phase.
items: Discovery: a requirements summary and a project roadmap
Sitemap, page structure and key flows, approved before visual work
Interface design: visual mockups and responsive layouts
Development on a live preview link
Testing, hosting setup and deployment to production
Source code and documentation, handed over to you

separate.title: Billed separately
separate.lead: Each appears as its own line, so nothing is folded into the build figure.
items: Domain, hosting and business email, each on its own line
Paid third-party services your build uses, such as payment gateways or SMS, billed when used
Revision work beyond the included rounds, at the published hourly rate
Scope added after the proposal, documented and agreed in writing first
A maintenance plan, only if you choose one

close.title: Get your range, or talk it through.
close.lead: The estimator gives an indicative range in a few minutes, with no contact details. A call is for when you'd rather describe the project out loud. Either way, the proposal is the only binding figure.

scopeNotes.title: What does it need?
scopeNotes.lead: Tick what applies. Each one is checked with you in scope review.
scopeNotes.badge: Confirmed in scope review — doesn't change this range

result.pending: Not answered — every option still counted
result.monthly: billed monthly or yearly, outside this range
result.disclaimer: Indicative only — not a quotation. The final price is set in a written proposal after scope review, valid for {days} days. {vat}

read.title: Preliminary read
read.basis: Based on what you've entered — a likely reading, not a verdict.

drivers.brand: A brand identity built from scratch

read.noDrivers: Mostly the project type and complexity you chose; none of your other answers pushes it up.

next.consultation: Likely a consultation first. Web apps, extensive builds, payments or integrations, and urgent timelines are easier to scope in a conversation than in a form.
next.review: Likely a written scope review. Send these answers, we confirm scope with you, then fix one figure.

form.intro: We review your answers, confirm scope with you, and send one written figure.
form.name: Name
form.attached: Your answers and scope notes are attached to the request.

errors.phoneEmpty: A phone number is needed so we can confirm scope with you.
errors.phoneInvalid: Enter a phone or WhatsApp number — digits, spaces, + and - only.
errors.email: Check the email address, or leave it empty.

form.success: Request received. We will review your answers and contact you to confirm scope.
